chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:

I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when Abū Baṣīr said to him, “May I be your ransom, which night is the one in which one hopes for what is hoped for?” He said, “On the night of the twenty-first or the twenty-third.” He said, “If I am not able to manage both of them?” He said, “How easy two nights are for what you seek.”

He said: I said, “Sometimes we see the crescent among us, and someone comes to us informing us of the contrary in another land.” He said, “How easy four nights are regarding what you seek in them.” I said, “May I be your ransom, is the twenty-third night the night of al-Juhanī?” He said, “Indeed, that is what is said.”

I said, “May I be your ransom, Sulaymān ibn Khālid narrated that on the nineteenth the delegation of the pilgrims is written.” He said, “O Abā Muḥammad, the delegation of the pilgrims is written on Laylat al-Qadr, and deaths, afflictions, provisions, and what will occur until its like in the coming year. So seek it on the twenty-first and twenty-third, pray one hundred rakʿahs on each of them, keep both of them awake in worship if you are able until the light, and perform ghusl on them.”

He said: I said, “What if I am not able to do that while standing?” He said, “Then pray while you are sitting.” I said, “What if I cannot?” He said, “Then on your bed.” I said, “What if I cannot?” He said, “There is no harm on you that you take a little sleep at the beginning of the night. Indeed, the gates of the heaven are opened in the month of Ramaḍān, the devils are shackled, and the deeds are accepted—the deeds of the believers. Excellent is the month, the month of Ramaḍān. It used to be called in the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ‘al-Marzūq.’”

key_terms.الْبَلَايَا: trials and afflictions destined to occur
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, distinguished by mercy and acceptance of deeds
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ: Laylat al-Qadr, the night in which decrees for the coming year are written
key_terms.وَفْدُ الْحَاجِّ: the delegation of the pilgrims whose affair is recorded

ai.seo_question: Which nights of Ramaḍān should Laylat al-Qadr be sought in according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies the twenty-first and twenty-third nights of Ramaḍān as the nights in which Laylat al-Qadr is to be sought, and it encourages worship on both nights. It also mentions recommended acts on these nights, including salat, staying awake in worship, and ghusl, while allowing ease for those unable to perform them fully.
